newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia expects more Italian investment.
newsitem.headline: Croatia expects more Italian investment.

text.p: Croatia expects more investments from its Adriatic neighbour Italy, whose Prime Minister Romano Prodi visited the Croatian capital on Thursday to boost the economic cooperation between the two countries.
State news agency HINA quoted Croatian PM Zlatko Matesa as saying Italy was Croatia's main trade partner, as their annual trade amounted to $2.5 billion.

"The level of trade (with Italy) is enviable and we can see a transition from trade to higher forms of cooperation, such as investment into Croatia and banking," Matesa told state television after meeting Prodi.
Prodi, accompanied by a high-level business delegation, also met Croatian president Franjo Tudjman, cardinal Franjo Kuharic and a group of Croatian businessmen.
Prodi said Italy lent full support to investments into Croatia's economy, adding that infrastructure, telecommunications and banking were the main areas of investment.
He also said Italy was keen to extend the cooperation on the Adriatic, including fishing, ecology and sea research projects.

Croatia is waiting for credit rating from three leading rating agencies. The rating, widely expected to be solid, is to be announced later on Thursday or Friday and should boost foreign investment. (( -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557 075))
